a_near_miss_worth_recording: The first arXiv attempt returned HTTP 301 with 0 bytes because the API now requires HTTPS. The parser reported it as no results. Had that been taken at face value it would have become a false white-space claim built on a FAILED REQUEST - precisely the failure mode round 1's own standard warns about ('I did not find anything' is not evidence). It was caught by checking the raw response instead of trusting the empty parse.
adjacent_fields_found: File fragment TYPE classification - which format a fragment belongs to. Fragments-Expert and related work. Shares the carved-fragment setting but asks a different question.
JPEG and MPEG double-compression detection - established media forensics. Shares the 'recover encoding history' shape but on a different medium and with the container available.
domain: Carved-DEFLATE encoder provenance (implementation + level from a mid-stream fragment)
honest_limits: encode.su, the venue where compression practitioners actually argue, is unreachable from this container (403) and was NOT searched. That is the single most likely place for undocumented prior work on this exact question, and its absence is a real gap in this check.
'File fragment classification' is adjacent enough that a reader could reasonably call it closer than this assessment does. The papers are named so that judgement can be made independently.
No patent search was run. Round 4 found two USPTO patents on a different candidate's exact task, so patents are a demonstrated blind spot for this kind of check.

verdict.reading: The second G4 clause - NO OPEN DATASET AT TARGET SCALE - is confirmed first-hand and is the clause that decides whether there is something to BUILD. Zero datasets at any scale, in the two indices where such a dataset would live. The first clause is weaker: five non-learned tools exist and are named, so this is not an unstudied problem. Under the effort lens that is the point rather than a problem - a published tool is evidence the mechanism works.

why: Everything now rests on this candidate - EphemErr died at A2 and the graveyard is exhausted - and the white-space claim had only ever been made by a round-1 subagent. Round 2 taught that an empty arXiv result can reflect a community's publishing habits rather than an empty field, so this was re-run first-hand.
